classification_scope._doctrine: A data class describes WHAT ENTERS THE PROMPT and WHERE THE OUTPUT GOES. It does not describe the subject the scientist works on. This distinction is the difference between a router people use and a router people go around.
classification_scope.in_prompt: Classify on the material actually pasted, attached, or retrieved into the model's context. Asking how to configure a tool, which parameters matter, or why a pipeline behaves a certain way puts NO regulated data in the prompt, however regulated the underlying study is.
classification_scope.destination: Classify up if the output lands in a regulatory submission, a GxP record, a safety case, or a decision about an identified person. Destination can raise a class that origin alone would not.
classification_scope.worked_example: 'Write a Nextflow workflow for our WGS joint-genotyping run' is research-unpub or public: no sequence enters the prompt. 'Here are 200 variant calls from our cohort, interpret them' is germline-seq: the sequence is in the prompt. Same study, same scientist, different class, and the router must not conflate them.
classification_scope.public_carve_out: Material that is already public and openly consented for unrestricted secondary use stays at its own class and is NOT escalated by subject matter. Openly consented public reference resources are the standard example. The escalate-when-arguable rule applies to genuine ambiguity about YOUR data, never to published reference data.

data_classes.label: Unpublished preclinical research, no human subjects
Trade secret: chemical matter, sequences, process know-how
Clinical data, de-identified under HIPAA (still GDPR personal data)
Human sequence data in the prompt: germline reads, genotypes or variant calls, including the normal arm of a tumour-normal pair
data_classes.note: Sequence is re-identifying in its own right and it identifies relatives who never consented, so removing identifiers does not lower the class. HIPAA's eighteen Safe Harbor identifiers do not list sequence data, which is a recognised gap in the rule rather than a permission; GDPR Article 9 names genetic data explicitly.

scope.applies_when: Human sequence data enters the prompt: reads, genotypes, VCF records, or per-individual variant lists.
scope.somatic_and_tumour_normal: Somatic work is IN SCOPE where the germline is present. A tumour-normal pair contains a germline sample by construction, and a tumour-only call set still carries germline variants that were never filtered out. Classify a somatic workflow here unless the material in the prompt is demonstrably germline-free.
does_not_apply_when: No sequence enters the prompt. Pipeline configuration, parameter choice, tool comparison, error interpretation and code review about a genomics study are research-unpub or public. See classification_scope; blocking these is the fastest way to push genomics work onto a personal account.
The sequence is from a public resource that is openly consented for unrestricted secondary use. That is public, and it does not escalate.
The material is aggregate to a level where no individual genotype is recoverable. Which aggregations qualify, at what cohort size, is open item 10 and is the DPO's determination, not the requester's.
scope.tier_is_itself_an_open_question: Placed at tier 7, above clin-deid because the identifiers cannot be removed, and below clin-id only because a sequence without a linked clinical record needs an external reference panel to attribute. If your consent forms or your Data Use Agreements treat sequence as identifiable on its face, this belongs at tier 8. See open item 10.

continuity_flags._doctrine: A platform can be withdrawn from an operating division on a day's notice. Two reported events anchor this: a vendor pulled government-wide in February 2026, switched off at one department in March and restored by injunction in April; and a production regulatory system re-pointed to another vendor on roughly seventy-two hours' notice, requiring re-engineering and revalidation of a retrieval pipeline. BOTH ARE TAGGED UNVERIFIED as claims C1 and C2 in docs/CLAIMS-REGISTER.md - they are reports, not findings, and the vendor-specific detail in C1 must not be repeated outside the company. The doctrine stands without them: availability is a contract variable, so any workflow that would be an emergency to move needs a written alternate before it goes to production, not after.

claude-ent.text: Demonstrated availability interruption during 2026 in the federal context, restored by injunction, with litigation open. Commercial terms differ from federal ones, but the precedent is that availability is a contract variable and not a given. Any production workflow on this platform carries a verified alternate and a continuity reserve. NOTE: the availability claim behind this flag is C1 in docs/CLAIMS-REGISTER.md and is UNVERIFIED. A `watch` level on a named vendor is a commercially consequential statement; source it or drop the vendor-specific narrative before this leaves the company.

openai-ent.text: No availability interruption on record in this estate. Model-version deprecation cadence is the live risk rather than withdrawal: a workflow pinned to a deprecated version is a swap with a deadline.

gemini-ent.text: Model-version deprecation cadence is the live risk.

copilot.text: Tenant-coupled. The continuity risk is a tenant or licensing change rather than a vendor action.
